correctness.rationale: For each strict sign pattern, fixed-neighborhood \(C^1\) convergence to an affine normalized within-sign Laplacian flow is justified by the nonzero confidence gap. The limiting Jacobian is similar to a strictly negative-definite matrix, so local hyperbolic persistence yields all \(2^n\) stable branches and exact first-order expansion through \(I+L_{\mathrm{same}}\). The zero state is an exact equilibrium with strictly stable limiting Jacobian because delta>1. In the scalar three-agent case, piecewise uniform limits exclude roots except near a=sqrt(delta)-1 and 1; every root near a is shown to cross upwards, making it unique, while near 1 the derivative is negative, giving exactly five roots and their basin signs. The logarithmic root equation and outer logistic tail establish both asymptotic coefficients. Python checks found 324 stable graph configurations, fifteen double-precision scalar cases, and twelve independent arbitrary-precision scalar cases. Finite verification is supportive rather than an infinite proof. The fixed-cutoff and sufficiently-large-steepness qualifiers are essential.

originality.rationale: The primary paper defines the same normalized logistic dynamics and proves necessary limiting relationships and special-topology stability statements. Its Conjecture 1 explicitly poses reverse HK-to-smooth equilibrium approximation, while its Section 5 says arbitrary topology equilibrium classification remains open. The present proof supplies persistent, hyperbolic attracting smooth equilibria for every binary labeling on an arbitrary persuadable graph under an explicitly fixed complete two-zealot exposure pattern, with an exponential \(2^n+1\) lower bound and a nontrivial \(I+L_{\mathrm{same}}\) inverse displacement law. The special \(n=1\) exactly-five-equilibria and basin-wall asymptotics are not implied by the existing necessary limit theorem or by its central-state stability theorem. Checked related nonlinear consensus and opinion sensitivity papers involve different dynamics. Extensive actual source/result searches and comparison of implication directions revealed no covering theorem; residual indexed-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: No negative search result proves priority: an unindexed equivalent binary-attractor theorem or unpublished application of hyperbolic continuation remains possible.
Other large-steepness equilibria might exist, so the \(2^n+1\) count is not asserted exhaustive for \(n\ge2\).
The scope of the source Conjecture 1 is much broader than this special positive lifting instance.

value.rationale: The count answers a motivated question in the specific smoothed bounded-confidence model: how many attracting persistent-disagreement configurations survive very sharp confidence filtering when EVERY persuadable agent hears both rival zealots? It shows exponential multiplicity for an arbitrary, even complete, persuadable graph, contrary to any simple expectation that dense cross-group ties enforce a unique attractor. The inverse within-camp Laplacian correction quantifies how actual graph topology shifts polarized opinions at finite sharpness; the exact minimal nontrivial case identifies basin walls, not merely equilibrium existence. These are natural quantitative refinements linked directly to the source paper’s unresolved reverse HK approximation question, rather than arbitrary small numerical gains. This is not claimed to settle the full conjecture, classify all higher-dimensional states, or predict real-world prevalence.
